newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Korea's LTCB to issue floating Kangaroo-CBA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Korea's LTCB to issue floating Kangaroo-CBA.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia said it has been mandated to lead manage a A$125 million kangaroo floating rate note issue for Korea Long Term Credit Bank.
The three-year offering is the first FRN under the kangaroo structure, which is foreign debt raising in the Australian domestic market.
Wayne Hoy, Chief Manager Commonwealth Bank Financial Markets, said the transaction is a milestone for Australian capital markets.

"This latest mandate demonstrates both the increasing sophistication of the domestic market towards accepting foreign risk and growing recognition amongst quality Asian borrowers that Australia provides cost effective alternative to other capital markets in the region," Hoy said.
CBA, which led a A$150 million fixed rate kangaroo bond for Korea Development Bank in August, expects to launch the new issue by the end of next week and will be free of Australian withholding tax.

"We expect the floating rate note will be an attractive instrument in the current interest rate environment. Early feedback indicates positive feedback to the name, product, price and maturity," said Ian Burnett, CBA's head of Global Fixed Interest Distribution.
The indicated spread is 20-21 basis points over bank bills, he added.
"Korea's imminent entry into the OECD enhances the appeal of the issue with Korean bank risk weightings set to fall to 20 percent from a present weighting of 100 percent," he said.
Moo Kyung Kan, Team Leader International Treasury Department at the Korean bank, said the issue will allow it to broaden its investor base and diversify its funding.

On Thursday Bankers Trust Australia said it is lead managing a fixed rate kangaroo bond for Korea Exchange Bank, which is expected to be around A$180 million and maturing December 1999. Pricing is expected to yield 37-40 basis points over the Australia government July 99 bond.-Sydney newsroom 61-2 373-1800
